did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, the Lord is described as removing from Jerusalem and Judah not only their leaders, but also their “support of bread” and “support of water”—that is, their basic necessities.
Did you know? The list of leaders the Lord will remove includes a mighty man, a warrior, a judge, a prophet, a diviner, and an elder—a wide range of people with authority and responsibility.
Did you know? Isaiah describes the collapse of leadership: instead of experienced leaders, “boys” will rule the people, and “children” will govern them.

Did you know? When one man asks his brother to become a leader and take responsibility, he refuses, saying that his household has neither bread nor clothing—an expression of poverty and unwillingness to lead.
Did you know? The chapter explicitly connects the fall of Jerusalem and Judah with their words and deeds, which are described as rebellion against the Lord and an insult to his glory.

Did you know? The chapter presents a principle of personal retribution: the righteous are told that it will go well with them and that they will enjoy the fruit of their deeds, while the wicked will receive what their actions deserve.
Did you know? The Lord is described as standing to contend and ready to judge the peoples; the judgment is directed especially at the elders and leaders of the people.
Did you know? The leaders of the people are accused of devouring the vineyard—a symbolic image of harming the people—and of keeping what they have taken from the poor in their own houses.
Did you know? The chapter’s criticism of the daughters of Zion focuses on their pride, their arrogant walk, their glances, and their behavior intended to attract attention.

Did you know? The punishment includes the removal of a very wide range of jewelry, clothing, and beauty accessories; instead of perfume, belts, and beauty there will be decay, baldness, sackcloth, and shame.
Did you know? The chapter ends by describing the city’s men falling by the sword in battle, and Jerusalem’s entrances mourning and deserted as the city sits humbled to the ground.
